developing a model for simulating transport phenomena in continuous castings.

the development of a comprehensive model for the simulation of the continuous casting of a billet.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present macroscopic modeling approach is capable of simulating the phase transition process and transport of the solid fraction in the mold region of the continuous casting process, in presence of EM-stirring.
the model predictions are in good agreement with available experimental and numerical results.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the model can be used to study the influence of process parameters on the phase change process, and to design a suitable casting process for the production of billets with desired solid fraction distribution.
the model can be used for simulating the macroscopic transport processes during continuous casting of non dendritic billets.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the model predicts a significant increase in the cooling rate in the presence of electromagnetic stirring, as a result of the increase in the effective heat transfer coefficient at the mold-billet interface.
the electromagnetic stirring is a very powerful tool for improving the quality of the cast product.
